correctness.rationale: Both exact complete traversals check 2^20 landmark subsets and compare all 30 five-level edge-distance histograms: one via BFS on the 2/3-subset inclusion graph and bitmasked shell intersections, the other via a separate GP(10,3) presentation and Gray-code updates. Both give only 720 at size eight, 960 at ten and 720 at twelve. The 720-mask certificate is regenerated byte-identically, and the S5 times C2 action partitions it into three 240-element orbits whose induced-edge counts are 4,5,6. The full-vertex edge histogram is identically (2,4,8,4,2), proving the complement duality. All arithmetic is exact and the search is exhaustive, not sampled.

originality.rationale: The 2023 foundational paper establishes the edge-multiset invariant but does not compute its Desargues-graph resolving spectrum. Its sufficient no-resolution condition for all vertex-to-edge distances at most two is inapplicable because this graph attains level four. The hypercube study treats a different graph family. Ordinary edge-metric scalar results and other Desargues parameters do not imply a multiset coefficient census. Research-record queries for Desargues, its GP(10,3) representation, and its bipartite-Kneser name found no covering statement, subject to unindexed-priority risk.

value.rationale: Complete identification-set enumeration for the canonical twenty-vertex Desargues incidence graph gives a sharply nonmonotone three-layer polynomial, excludes every odd cardinality, exhibits complementary resolving sets and classifies all 720 minima into three inequivalent geometric orbits. The nonmonotone failure of adding any one landmark contrasts with ordered edge-metric resolution and supplies a precise benchmark for this newer graph invariant. This is more than a scalar or routine parameter increment.
